intervals.label: collaboration
intervals.note: The collaboration's founding date is not published in the sources read; 2005 is the first chamber installation (and Fermilab news says work began at Fermilab in 2005). The end is the merger into PICO (see the completed row).
intervals.quote: Early in 2005 we installed a chamber containing 1.5 kg of CF3 I, an industrial refrigerant commonly used as a fire extinguisher, at the 350-foot depth of the NuMI (Neutrinos at the Main Injector) tunnel in Fermilab.

intervals.label: completed (merged into PICO)
intervals.note: Year precision: arXiv:1304.6001 (April 2013) is still signed 'COUPP Collaboration'; this talk abstract (13 November 2013) already calls it 'the former COUPP collaboration'. The merger date itself is not published in the sources read.
intervals.quote: I will discuss a suite of bubble chambers for dark matter detection in various stages of development by the former COUPP collaboration and the new PICO collaboration, formed by the merger of COUPP and PICASSO.

name: COUPP Collaboration
notes: Lineage into PICO: COUPP and PICASSO merged to form the PICO Collaboration (see collaboration:pico and the log's 'for the integrator' list).
No collaboration website was found (the COUPP pages at Fermilab are not in the sources read); no roster or member count is recorded.

summary.plain: The team around Fermilab, the University of Chicago and Indiana University South Bend that built bubble chambers to search for dark matter. By late 2013 it had merged with PICASSO to form the PICO Collaboration.
summary.technical: COUPP (Chicagoland Observatory for Underground Particle Physics) operated CF3I bubble chambers of 1.5 kg (2005, NuMI tunnel), 3.5-4 kg (MINOS tunnel at Fermilab, then SNOLAB) and the 60 kg chamber later run as PICO-60. The last papers signed 'COUPP Collaboration' date from April 2013; by November 2013 PICO describes COUPP as 'the former COUPP collaboration'. No formation date or roster is published in the sources read.
